To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a functional gene network is a powerful and generalizable predictor of mammalian gene function, and the combination of a functional gene network and a classifier is a powerful predictor of gene function.
the functional gene network approach outperformed a classification approach, and their combination offered some improvement over either individually.

a network-based approach is generally more predictive of functional gene annotations than a classifier-based approach and that a network approach is more useful in predicting the functional annotations of genes that are not well connected to other characterized genes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
inferring gene functions from large-scale data.
the problem of predicting the functions of mammalian genes from genomic-scale data, with the goal of producing a large-scale functional network of mouse genes and a high-confidence subset.
the problem of predicting the functions (GeneOntology annotations) of uncharacterized mammalian genes from a variety of genomic data sources.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the network approach is better than the classifier approach, and that their combination is better still, for predicting the functional annotation of mouse genes.
the MouseFunc data and the methods we have developed for mining the data provide an excellent starting point for further development of functional genomics in mammals.
, while there is no one single best approach to functional annotation inference, there is much room for improvement and that a combination of approaches is likely to be the best path forward.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the network-based strategy is more powerful than the classifier-based approach, and the combined approach is more powerful than either alone, but that all three strategies are complementary and should be used in concert for functional genomics analyses.

we developed a functional network of mouse genes that is predictive of gene function, and that we demonstrated that a combination of network-based and classifier-based approaches is a promising path for predicting mammalian gene function.

, with a combined functional network and classification strategy, we were able to produce functional annotations for 1,339 genes in a mouse test set with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.85, a median average precision of 19.5%, and a median area under a ROC curve for the top 50 predictions of 0.92.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MouseFunc competition has been a successful effort to stimulate the development of computational tools for functional genomics.
a combined network/classifier strategy for inferring gene function can be quite successful, and that the network-based strategy can provide a useful resource for functional genomics.

, while there is still a great deal of work to be done towards understanding the functions of the mammalian genome, the data and computational approaches are now sufficiently mature to provide a high-confidence functional network of mammalian genes.
